reasoning_traces.think:
The PU-index quantifies the "surprise" of the true class given the classifier's output. For a perfectly calibrated binary classifier, u_i follows a Beta(α, α) distribution with α = 1, yielding E[u_i] = 0.5. When the test distribution shifts, the classifier becomes overconfident on old patterns and underconfident on new ones, causing E[u_i] to increase. This primitive is dual to the calibration error in Bayesian posterior checking and the nonconformity measure in conformal inference.
